title: NN/g placeholder text usability in forms
statement:
NN/g's user testing found placeholder text used as a field label or hint hurts usability (it disappears, strains memory, prevents checking entries, is skipped as if already filled in, and is often low-contrast or unread by screen readers), so lead-capture and sign-up forms should use visible labels and hints outside the field.

Options:
- Label and hint outside: Visible label above each field, with any essential hint also visible outside the field (fits: clear, trustworthy, professional)
- Label plus optional example: Label outside the field plus a placeholder used only for a non-essential example (fits: practical, friendly, modern)
- Floating label compromise: Floating labels that move above the field on focus, as a space-saving compromise on mobile (still leaves some issues NN/g describes) (fits: minimal, mobile-first, modern)
- Programmatically linked hints: Persistent helper text linked to the input with aria-describedby (fits: accessible, technical, careful)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general, seniors.

source.title: Placeholders in Form Fields Are Harmful
